To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure and the properties of the poly(urea formadehyde) microcapsules are dependent on the reaction time, reaction temperature, and monomers/PCM ratio, which are the key parameters of the encapsulation process.

the structure of microcapsules depends strongly on reaction time, and that the content of encapsulated RT 42 increased by increasing reaction temperature until an optimum temperature was reached, and finally that the optimal monomer/PCM ratio was 0,8.

the structure of generated poly(ureas formaldehyde) microencapsulated paraffins strongly depends on the reaction time; the content of encapsulated paraffin increased with the reaction temperature until a certain limit; and finally the optimum mass ratio of the monomers/PCM was 0.80.

a simple, efficient, and low-cost method for the encapsulation of RT 42 parafin in poly(urea) microcapsules, which can be used as a thermal energy storage system.

the preparation of poly(urea) formaldehyde microcapsules containing a PCM.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the in situ polymerization is a suitable technique for encapsulation of the paraffin wax in poly(urea formadehyde).
the optimum microcapsule preparation conditions are prepolymerization time 1 h, polymerization time 2 h, reaction temperature 70 degC, and monomers/RT 42 mass ratio of 0.8.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the microcapsules containing RT 42 parafin can be used in thermal energy storage systems and that the microcapsule shell thickness is an important parameter for the thermal energy storage capacity of the microcapsule.
it is possible to prepare poly(urea formadehyde) microcapsules with a high content of paraffin by in situ polymerization of urea and formaldehyde.
